title: The waltz keeps coming back
work: Waltz in C♯ minor, Op. 64 No. 2
question: How do these four pianists make the circling tune answer the slower melodies?
intro: Paderewski, Pachmann, Rummel and Gurevich begin with the same small tension: a melody that lingers while the bass keeps dancing. Chopin sets quick quavers running between that C♯-minor song and a gentler one in D♭ major. The circling refrain keeps returning, and gets the last word.

recordings.label: Ignacy Jan Paderewski, 1917
recordings.note: Paderewski’s Victor recordings preserve his habit of spreading chords and letting the melody arrive separately from the bass.

recordings.label: Vladimir de Pachmann, 1925
recordings.note: Pachmann plays his own Baldwin at Hayes, with his own variant in bars 82–83.

recordings.label: Walter Morse Rummel, 1943
recordings.note: Rummel had introduced Debussy’s complete second book of Préludes in London in 1913.

recordings.label: Olga Gurevich, c. 2014
recordings.note: Gurevich grew up studying piano in Baku; her teachers’ ideal of a singing tone remains central to her own teaching.

passages.label: Opening waltz
passages.note: Held notes lean across the bar line, then a quick curl answers them. The bass keeps its note-and-two-chords step.

passages.label: The phrase takes breath
passages.note: The opening melody finishes another turn, its short flourishes tucked between longer notes; the waltz accompaniment keeps going.

passages.label: The quavers start running
passages.note: The right hand starts running in chains of quavers, marked più mosso — more movement. The left hand keeps dancing beneath it.

passages.label: Falling and rising
passages.note: The quick tune falls, climbs back and falls again, fitting its curls across the left hand’s three-beat pattern.

passages.label: A song in D♭ major
passages.note: The piano turns to D♭ major and a broader melody. Più lento asks for a slower pace.

passages.label: The opening melody returns
passages.note: The opening C♯-minor melody returns, with its held notes and little answering flourishes, before the quick refrain has the final say.
